name: Moli OS
description: Moli OS is an agent-native, ultra-light home automation platform written in Rust: one static binary that embeds its dashboard, with drivers for Zigbee2MQTT, Hue, Tuya, Sonos, Reolink, Frigate and more, a deterministic automation engine, and MCP, REST and CLI access for AI agents under a human guard. This script installs the release binary of the fork, runs it as a systemd service under its own user, and keeps the vault's master key outside the data directory.

notes.text: There is no default account. At first start Moli writes a one-hour setup code to its log (journalctl -u moli-os | grep code=). Open http://<IP>:8790, type it, then choose the house code. Whoever types that code first claims the house, and a new code is written at every start until then, so finish the setup right after the install.

The vault's master key is /etc/moli-os/master.key, created once at install. Backups (moli-os backup) never contain it: keep a copy in a password manager. Never generate a new one on an existing house: its vault would become unreadable.
Run moli-os commands from the container's root shell as `moli-os <command>` (for example moli-os check-config): the wrapper runs them as the service user with the service's configuration and key.
Every update backs up the data to /var/backups/moli-os, keeps the previous binary as /opt/moli-os/moli-os.previous, and goes back to it on its own if /api/health does not answer.
